title: OntologyBench: Can Dense Retrieval Satisfy Structured Biomedical Constraints?
abstract: arXiv:2609.08174v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We introduce OntologyBench, a tiered biomedical retrieval benchmark comprising 471,854 training and 125,744 evaluation query-document relevance pairs across concept grounding, relational retrieval, and compositional phenotype-based retrieval.   Although these tasks can be tractable using ontology-aware reference methods, across task tiers, embedding performance is generally lower on relational and compositional tasks than on concept-grounding tasks. Fine-tuning on ontology-derived supervision improves performance on several relational and compositional tasks, whereas the evaluated reranking and LLM-based candidate-scoring methods provide little or no end-to-end improvement. Errors frequently reflect diseases matching only subsets of the phenotype evidence.   These findings indicate that the evaluated embedding and reranking configurations do not reliably recover the compatibility encoded by the selected ontology relations and phenotype c

translated_title: OntologyBench：稠密检索能否满足结构化生物医学约束？
translated_abstract: 我们提出了OntologyBench，这是一个分层的生物医学检索基准，包含471,854个训练和125,744个评估用查询-文档相关性对，涵盖概念定位、关系检索和基于表型的组合检索三类任务。尽管使用本体感知的参考方法可以处理这些任务，但跨各任务层级来看，嵌入模型在关系型和组合型任务上的表现普遍低于概念定位任务。基于本体派生监督的微调可以提升若干关系型和组合型任务的性能，而所评估的重排序方法及基于大语言模型（LLM）的候选评分方法则几乎没有或完全没有带来端到端的改进。错误往往反映出疾病仅匹配了表型证据的一部分。这些发现表明，所评估的嵌入和重排序配置无法可靠地恢复由所选本体关系和表型约束所编码的兼容性。
tldr: 提出分层生物医学检索基准OntologyBench，揭示当前稠密检索嵌入模型在满足本体关系和表型组合等结构化约束方面仍存在显著不足。
en_tdlr: OntologyBench, a tiered biomedical retrieval benchmark, reveals that current dense retrieval embeddings fail to reliably satisfy structured constraints encoded by ontology relations and phenotype-based compositional requirements.
